references.text: Moses tells the people that the Lord will give them meat to eat in the evening and bread to satisfy them in the morning, as a test of their obedience to the Lord's laws.

In the evening, quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was dew around the camp. When the dew had lifted, there was something fine and flaky on the desert floor, fine like frost on the ground.
The house of Israel called it manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers with honey.
On the evenings when the people complained about the lack of meat, Moses prayed to the Lord, who answered that the people would receive meat, so much that it would become repulsive to them.
The Lord rained down manna for food and gave them grain from heaven. People ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.
An invitation to all who are thirsty to come to the water, even those without money, to buy and eat. The Lord asks why they spend money on what is not bread and their labor on what does not satisfy.
Jesus feeds four thousand men, besides women and children, with seven loaves of bread and a few small fish.
Jesus feeds five thousand men with five loaves of bread and two fish.
